awards.why: Nearly 35,000 reviews at 4.6 stars for about $15, with fade-on and gentle-off built in.

awards.label: Best for Alexa Homes
awards.why: Sets up entirely in the Alexa app, no extra app needed, for $16.99.

awards.label: Best for 3-Way

products.verdict: The best-selling smart dimmer on Amazon. Cheap, reliable, and the Kasa app is easy to use.
pros: 34,939 reviews at 4.6 stars, 2K+ bought in the past month
Fade on with a click, gentle fade off with a double click
cons: Single-pole only; the 3-way version is the KS230 kit

products.verdict: Kasa's 3-way dimmer kit for stairs and hallways, with 1% to 100% dimming.
pros: 2,633 reviews, 2K+ bought in the past month

products.verdict: A well-rated budget dimmer with 1,718 reviews at 4.5 stars.
cons: Only FCC listed; no safety certification named

products.verdict: The simplest dimmer for an Alexa home. Setup and control happen entirely in the Alexa app.
pros: No extra app, set up in the Alexa app

products.verdict: A single dimmer that handles single-pole, 3-way, and 4-way circuits, with a level indicator on the face.
cons: A licensed electrician is recommended in the listing
Feit app only, no Home Assistant integration

products.verdict: Kasa's Apple Home version in a three-pack, so iPhone users get Siri and the Home app without Matter.
pros: Works in Apple Home with Siri
Also works with Alexa and Google
cons: Apple Home remote access needs a home hub

products.verdict: Four Tapo dimmers for about $13 each. The cheapest way to do several rooms.
pros: 1% to 100% dimming by touch, app, or voice

products.verdict: A touch-slider dimmer with an adjustable brightness range to stop low-end flicker.
pros: Adjustable minimum brightness to fix flicker

products.verdict: One of the few Wi-Fi-controlled dimmers that installs without a neutral. It needs Leviton's MLWSB bridge.
pros: Works with Alexa, Google, Apple Home, SmartThings, and Sonos
Wire-free 3-way with a Leviton Anywhere companion
Preset levels, fade rates, and bulb-type settings
cons: Requires the MLWSB Wi-Fi bridge, sold separately

products.verdict: Leviton's Wi-Fi Decora dimmer with min-dim and max-bright settings for flicker-free LEDs.
pros: Adjustable bulb type, minimum dim, and maximum bright
Night settings for softer light at night
cons: Listing doesn't cover neutral, 3-way, or voice assistants
Costs more than Kasa or Tapo

avoid.flag: 75 W LED limit per its own listing, 3.5 stars
avoid.verdict: Two dimmers in one gang sounds handy, but the listing caps LED loads at 75 W, about half what a normal smart dimmer handles.
reasons: The listing's own note gives a maximum of 75 W of LED/CFL, so a few fixtures can overload it.
It can't run 3-way circuits, smart bulbs, or fans, per the listing.
